prerequisites: Knowledge of Circuit Theory and alternating current in three-phase systems.

learning_outcomes.text: For the student to know the principles governing the operation of electrical machines, their characteristics, their electromechanical model, and their use.
Understanding and interpretation of texts and data, development of skills for their concretization and clear and concise presentation.
Aptitude for the distribution of resources and time and their implementation in real situations.
Ability to use scientific-technical tools for solving calculation and design problems in Industrial Engineering and aptitude for finding sustainable engineering solutions.
Ability for teamwork and ability to develop multidisciplinary projects.
Knowledge and use of the principles of circuit theory and electrical machines.

syllabus_topics: Theory of magnetic circuits - Magnetic materials - Magnetic circuits - Magnetic energy - Alternating current and magnetism
Transformers - Real transformers - Accessories - The electrical model of the transformer - Tests - Special transformers
General principles of rotating electrical machines - Basic elements - Power, losses and efficiency - Magneto- and electro-motive forces - Classification of rotating machines
Asynchronous machines - Construction and operation - Equivalent circuit and tests - Torque, operating regime and efficiency - Starting and speed regulation
Synchronous machines - Construction and operation - The synchronous generator - Coupling and regulation - The synchronous motor
Other rotating machines - Direct current - The universal motor - Brushless DC motors - Stepper motors
Transformers: measurement of internal voltage drop.
Induction motor: no-load or free rotor test.
Induction motor: short-circuit or locked rotor test.
DC motor: starting and speed regulation.
Stepper motor: control using programmable microcontroller.
teaching_methods: Tutorials on topics raised in class
assessment_rules: The course evaluation is based on objective tests, where theory accounts for 50% and problems for 50%. Both the theory and problems components must be passed within each test. All parts of the assessment (e.g., partial and final exams) must be passed. The grade for each test is the average of its theory and problems components, provided both are passed. The final course grade is the average of these test grades, provided both parts have been passed.
